answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to lock a refundable stake that grows like a vine: reputation accrues slowly through verified work, and any proven fraud slashes the stake, like a comet burning its own tail. New identities start at zero trust, so spawning a thousand fresh agents costs a thousand stakes with no history to sell. Like water pooling in karst limestone, value only flows through channels carved over time, making cheap identity spam economically pointless.
